clue.text: A new scale on map of France

indicators.note: new here means made anew, so the letters of scale are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A cartographer has drawn France at a fresh scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns SCALE into SACLE, after A as written. The definition is loose: the region is something found on a map of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a region in north-eastern France, bordering Germany, so it appears on any map of the country.

clue.text: State, over long period, provides the means

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed over the second

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
ages means a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone claims that over a long period it all evens out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places AVER above AGES in the down grid. 'means' are mathematical averages, not money or methods.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic a mean is the sum divided by the count, so means are typical middle values.

clue.text: Jacket for philosopher — or poet, say

definitions.meaning: a short close-fitting jacket named after an earl
Herbert, the Victorian philosopher, bore this surname

explanation.surface: A jacket suitable for a thinker, or perhaps a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or poet, say' adds a third reading by sound: Edmund Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene, whose name is pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A short double-breasted waist jacket bears the name of an earl, and Herbert of that surname was a Victorian philosopher.

clue.text: Perhaps a Persian visitor is noisy protester

parts.note: a Persian is one breed of cat, with Perhaps showing an example
a caller is someone who visits

explanation.surface: A visitor from Persia turns out to be a loud demonstrator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persian' suggests a person from Iran, but it is the long-haired cat breed.
explanation.definitionFit: One who jeers or whistles in derision at a speaker is a heckler, a noisy protester.

clue.text: Undertaker for Scrooge

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
Ebenezer Scrooge, Dickens's tight-fisted character, is the archetypal miser

explanation.surface: A funeral director is working on behalf of a famous skinflint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertaker' looks like a funeral director, but here it means literally one who undertakes to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who undertakes a task gives a pledge, so is one who vows to do it.

clue.text: Engineers' double sculls race? Overhaul without stopping

parts.note: running is racing on foot
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineer corps
a double scull is a boat for a pair of rowers, so pairs

explanation.surface: Army engineers enter a double sculls rowing race.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the order race, Engineers, double sculls. Running repairs are minor fixes done while something stays in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor fixes made while a machine stays in service are a way of maintaining it continuously.

clue.text: Thomas turned over Kipling's work for theme

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the short name for Thomas is read backwards

parts.note: Tom is short for Thomas
If— is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: Thomas leafs through a Kipling book looking for its theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses TOM to MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring idea or figure in art or music is a theme.

clue.text: Bird's disputes

parts.note: to spar is to argue or dispute
a row is a dispute or quarrel

explanation.surface: A bird gets into squabbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disputes' gives two quarrel words in succession; 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The small brown-grey songbird is a common garden bird.

clue.text: Fellow closely resembling sexton

definitions.meaning: a dead ... is someone who looks exactly like another
a sexton's duties traditionally included tolling the church bell

explanation.surface: A lookalike of the churchwarden.
explanation.walkthrough: A sexton is a church caretaker, whose jobs included bell-ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: A double who looks just like someone else is called a dead one, and a bell-puller in a church is one too.

clue.text: In vain, lad tames awfully fierce animal

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of the words in vain lad tames are messed up

explanation.surface: A boy tries hopelessly to tame a savage beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges INVAINLADTAMES, all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The carnivorous marsupial of the Australian island state is known for its ferocity.

clue.text: Problem for observer entangled in tree, say

indicators.note: entangled means twisted up together, so the letters of the words in tree say are jumbled

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher caught up in a tree has a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangled' rearranges INTREESAY. The observer is anyone looking, whose eyes tire from overuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching eyes from too much looking are a typical complaint for anyone who watches closely.

clue.text: A literary pseudonym or two

definitions.meaning: Samuel Clemens wrote under the pen name Mark ...
an archaic word for a pair, as in 'never the ... shall meet'

explanation.surface: A pen name, or perhaps a pair of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Clemens adopted this surname as Mark's pen name, and it is also an old poetic word meaning a couple.

clue.text: Plaudits for a century? Right

definitions.note: a plural noun matched by a mass noun of the same sense

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
a right or entitlement to something is a claim on it

explanation.surface: A batsman scoring a hundred earns applause; is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a century is a score of 100 runs by one batsman, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiastic public praise and applause amount to the same thing as plaudits.

clue.text: Having legal validity among policemen

parts.note: among means in the midst of, so in
a police force is the body of policemen

explanation.surface: A rule counts as law among the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A law that is currently operative and enforceable is said to be valid and binding.

clue.text: Flynn at home in swashbuckler role

indicators.note: something at home in a place is lodged inside it, so the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The Hollywood star is comfortable playing a swashbuckling part.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in the last two letters of swashbuckler and finishes inside role.
explanation.definitionFit: Errol Flynn was the Hollywood actor famed for swashbuckling films such as Captain Blood, so his first name fits.

clue.text: Odd thing — birdie one's reluctant to turn in

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters of thing are rearranged

parts.note: an owl is a bird, birdie being a playful word for any bird

explanation.surface: Something strange: a little bird that doesn't want to go to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' turns THING into NIGHT. To turn in is to go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays up late and dislikes going to bed early is a habitual late-riser by nature.

clue.text: Move to another place in express, understandably

definitions.meaning: to shift something, such as a bishop to a new see, from one location to another
to put words into a language someone understands

explanation.surface: Relocating on an express train, which is understandable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the two meanings; 'express' is a verb, not a train.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to transfer something to a new location and to render words in another language so they are understood.

clue.text: Court's uncertain without king or queen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for uncertain goes around the royal letters

parts.note: chancy means risky or uncertain
ER stands for Edward Rex or Elizabeth Regina, so a king or a queen

explanation.surface: It is unclear whether a court operates with no monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking. Chancery is a division of the High Court in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancery Division is a branch of the English High Court, historically the Lord Chancellor's court.

clue.text: Want little time

parts.note: little in height means short
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A need for only a brief moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' is a noun here, meaning lack.
explanation.definitionFit: A want of something is a lack or insufficiency of it.

clue.text: Emperor gives 20 to Pope

parts.note: the answer to 20 across is the spelt-out name of the letter H
Adrian is the name of several popes, including the only English one

explanation.surface: An emperor hands a gift to the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' points to 20 across, whose answer names a letter, which goes first here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian was the Roman emperor who built the wall across northern Britain.

clue.text: In two cases, this character starts helping Holmes

definitions.text: In two cases, this character starts helping Holmes

parts.words: In two cases, this character starts helping Holmes
parts.note: the character is a letter of the alphabet, the one that begins both helping and Holmes, in upper and lower case, spelt out in full

explanation.surface: Someone joins Sherlock Holmes as his assistant on a pair of cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter, not a person, and 'cases' are upper and lower case, not detective cases.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter, which is the first letter of the words helping and Holmes.

clue.text: Period at home 'one finally ends

indicators.note: finally places the single letter for one at the very end of the build

parts.note: a term is a period, as in a school term
in means at home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A school term spent at home finally ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' is a plural noun here, the terminus stations or end points.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminal points or stations at the end of a line are its end points.

clue.text: Appropriate author

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning take for one's own use
George, the Victorian writer of Lavengro, had this surname

explanation.surface: A suitable writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something for temporary use is to appropriate it, and George of that name wrote Lavengro and The Bible in Spain.

clue.text: Veteran replaced in New Deal

indicators.note: replaced in says one word in the phrase is swapped for another, here its opposite

parts.note: a new deal of the cards gives the player a new hand

explanation.surface: An old soldier lost his job under Roosevelt's New Deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Deal was Roosevelt's 1930s programme; read as cards, it is a new hand, and replacing new with its opposite gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is a person long experienced at something, which is just what the idiom means.

clue.text: Apart from a simpleton, turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word for simpleton is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a fool is a simpleton

explanation.surface: Away from a dimwit who has just arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses FOOL to LOOF. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reserved and distant stands apart from others.

clue.text: Unsuccessful contestant was a smuggler as well

parts.note: as well means also, in addition
to run goods such as rum or guns is to smuggle them, so a smuggler ran them

explanation.surface: A loser in a competition also had a smuggling sideline.
explanation.walkthrough: To run contraband is an old sense of smuggling it.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or competitor who finishes unplaced in a race is the idiom for a loser.

clue.text: Brass animals

definitions.meaning: brass is British slang for money, and so is this old slang word
the plural can be the same as the singular for this horned African beast

explanation.surface: Animals cast in brass.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass and this word are both old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is old slang for money, as brass is, and it is the short form of the horned pachyderm's name, which can serve as its own plural.

clue.text: Flexible arrangement for relatives

indicators.note: an arrangement for some letters puts them in a new order, so relatives is reshuffled

explanation.surface: A family arrangement that can be adapted to suit any relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement for' rearranges RELATIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adaptable who can turn to many tasks is described as flexible.

clue.text: Unexpected bonus some, musicians decline

parts.note: the wind section is one group of musicians in an orchestra
to decline is to fall or drop

explanation.surface: Players refusing a surprise bonus payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' looks like refuse, but here means drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally fruit blown down by the wind, the word has come to mean any windfall of good luck such as an unforeseen gain.

clue.text: Girl's name, in fact

definitions.meaning: a female given name meaning truthfulness

explanation.surface: A girl's name, really.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a girl's name, and the word also means truth or a true fact, from Latin veritas.
